payload.public_summary: The specification is scientifically executable. The resolved model is N independent localized two-state units, each with nondegenerate energies 0 and Δ, so the derivation will produce Z_N=(1+e^{-βΔ})^N and the corresponding mean energy and heat capacity per particle.

specification_sections.name: purpose
specification_sections.content: Derive the canonical thermodynamics of N independent localized two-state units.

specification_sections.name: scientific_target
specification_sections.content: Obtain the N-unit canonical partition function, mean energy per particle, and heat capacity per particle as explicit functions of temperature T and level spacing Δ.

specification_sections.name: givens_and_starting_point
specification_sections.content: Each localized unit has two nondegenerate states with energies 0 and Δ, where Δ>0. The N units are distinguishable, independent, and in canonical equilibrium.

specification_sections.name: notation_and_conventions
specification_sections.content: Use β=1/(k_B T), retain k_B explicitly, denote the total mean energy by U, and define the internal heat capacity by C=dU/dT.

specification_sections.name: assumptions_and_regime
specification_sections.content: Use exact canonical Boltzmann weights for T>0. Because the units are independent, the N-unit partition function factorizes into the Nth power of the single-unit partition function. Temperature limits may be evaluated by continuity.

specification_sections.name: scope_and_non_goals
specification_sections.content: Include only the two internal levels. Exclude interactions, quantum exchange between units, translational motion, extra degeneracies or degrees of freedom, and any external-field or temperature dependence of Δ.

specification_sections.name: required_output
specification_sections.content: Construct the single-unit partition function and the factorized N-unit partition function Z_N=(1+e^{-βΔ})^N, then derive closed-form expressions for U/N and C/N as functions of T, Δ, and k_B.

specification_sections.name: validation_criteria
specification_sections.content: The expressions must be dimensionally consistent and give C/N≥0, U/N→0 and C/N→0 as T→0, and U/N→Δ/2 and C/N→0 as T→∞.

specification_sections.name: agent_discretion
specification_sections.content: The derivation agent may use exponential or hyperbolic-function forms, may derive observables through derivatives of ln Z_N or direct probabilities, and may include low- and high-temperature checks.

declared_defaults.title: Thermal units
declared_defaults.statement: Retain k_B explicitly and define β=1/(k_B T).
declared_defaults.rationale: This preserves physical dimensions and is immediately translatable to units with k_B=1.
alternatives: Use β as the sole temperature variable

declared_defaults.title: Heat-capacity notation
declared_defaults.statement: Interpret heat capacity as C=dU/dT for the internal two-level energy, equivalently C_V when volume is fixed.
declared_defaults.rationale: The stated model contains no volume-dependent energy.

declared_defaults.title: Temperature treatment
declared_defaults.statement: Use exact finite-temperature Boltzmann factors over both levels.
declared_defaults.rationale: The full requested temperature dependence is available in closed form without asymptotic approximation.

declared_defaults.title: Expression form
declared_defaults.statement: Treat exponential and hyperbolic-function forms as equivalent representations of the thermodynamic functions.
declared_defaults.rationale: These forms are algebraically interchangeable and encode identical physics.

refinement_ladder.name: Exact independent two-level result
refinement_ladder.relaxes: Baseline and final rung; it relaxes nothing and directly supplies the exact full-temperature deliverable for independent localized two-state units.
